limitations_and_boundaries: Pretraining data may not fully reflect the complexity of human organ development and health states.
Current model focuses on transcriptomic data only, not including genomic or epigenomic data.
Unsupervised pretraining does not leverage rich metadata information.
Batch effects or modality differences are left to cooperative downstream methods.
Users are recommended to use cell and gene embeddings rather than predicted gene expression values due to high dropout rates in labels.

research_questions.statement: Can a large-scale foundation model pretrained on single-cell transcriptomics achieve state-of-the-art performance across diverse downstream tasks?

provenance.text_excerpt: Here we developed a large pretrained model scFoundation ... with 100 million parameters covering about 20,000 genes, pretrained on over 50 million human single-cell transcriptomic profiles.

claims.statement: scFoundation is a large-scale foundation model with 100 million parameters pretrained on over 50 million human single-cell transcriptomic profiles, covering about 20,000 genes, and achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse downstream tasks including gene expression enhancement, drug response prediction, perturbation prediction, and cell type annotation.

provenance.text_excerpt: scFoundation achieved the highest macro F1 score on both datasets. Compared with the second-place method CellTypist, the higher performance of scFoundation came from improvements in rare cell types such as CD4+ T helper 2 and CD34+.

claims.statement: scFoundation achieved the highest macro F1 score on cell type annotation tasks (Zheng68K and TM datasets), with particular improvements in rare cell types.

scFoundation-based model for drug response prediction achieved high Pearson and Spearman correlations, with higher clustering scores (CH, SIL) compared to gene expression baseline, and enabled better transfer between bulk and single-cell data.

claims.statement: scFoundation outperformed imputation methods MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute, and scVI in clustering metrics NMI, ARI, and SIL on a human pancreatic islet dataset when T/S fold change was greater than 1.

datasets.description: Over 50 million human scRNA-seq profiles collected from GEO, Single Cell Portal, HCA, hECA, DISCO, EMBL-EBI and other public sources. Aligned to 19,264 protein-coding and common mitochondrial genes (HGNC). Spans over 100 tissue types across diseases, tumors and normal states.
datasets.name: scFoundation pretraining dataset

experiments_or_tasks: Develop scFoundation, a 100-million-parameter model covering 19,264 genes, pretrained on over 50 million human scRNA-seq profiles using the xTrimoGene architecture and RDA pretraining task.

methods.name: xTrimoGene architecture
methods.protocol_description: Scalable transformer-based model with embedding module and asymmetric encoder-decoder structure. Embedding module converts continuous gene expression scalars into learnable high-dimensional vectors. Encoder processes only nonzero and nonmasked gene embeddings plus T and S tokens. Decoder combines encoder output with mask and zero embeddings. Final MLP layer projects decoder output to expression values.

methods.name: RDA pretraining task
methods.protocol_description: For each cell, a hierarchical Bayesian downsampling strategy generates a low total counts variant. Normalize and log-transform both raw and input vectors. Define T (target total counts of raw sample) and S (source total counts of input sample). Randomly mask 30% of both zero and nonzero genes. Model predicts raw expression at masked positions using masked input plus T and S indicators. Loss is regression (MSE) on masked positions.
